surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Anderson has two goals and an assist as the Canadiens get past the Penguins
paras: The first period was a wild one. Erik Karlsson opened the scoring for the Penguins on the power play early in the period. Oliver Kapanen and Josh Anderson scored 24 seconds apart later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Tommy Novak made it 2-2 for Pittsburgh less than five minutes later. Montréal had a goal taken off for goalie interference midway through the first, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Alexandre Texier and Chris Kreider scored 27 seconds apart early in the second to put the Canadiens up 4-2. Rickard Rakell pulled the Penguins within one less than two minutes later, and Owen Beck and Blake Lizotte dropped the gloves midway through the period. Anderson scored his second of the night later in the period to make it 5-3 for the Canadiens, and that one stood up as the winner. With the goalie pulled and a little over three minutes left, Sidney Crosby made it 5-4, but the Habs held on. Three players had three-point nights: Crosby with a goal and two assists, Karlsson with a goal and two assists, and Anderson with two goals and an assist.

The Penguins had a little more of the play and hit two posts, but the Canadiens made their chances count. Jacob Fowler made 25 saves for the Canadiens, and Sergei Murashov allowed five goals on 27 shots. Fowler has won seven straight starts. By our Swing measure, Jake Evans had the best night of anyone. The Canadiens moved to 9-3-2, second in the Atlantic, while the Penguins fell to 5-7-2, sixth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Canadiens are rolling: five straight wins.
Chris Kreider scored again against Pittsburgh, and has seven goals in ten games against them since 2023-24.
Rickard Rakell has scored in three straight games.
The Penguins have gone winless in seven straight on the road.
